findings.title: Complement packing and lower-intruder resource cost
findings.claim: For integer q≥3, at most floor((q−1)/2) pairwise disjoint subsets of integers≥2 each sum to q; singleton {q} plus complementary pairs attain the bound. For k≥2 and m≥2k+2, this excludes the consecutive-lower-maximum forcing scheme on F(m,k): it requires k disjoint complements of q=k+2 but only floor((k+1)/2)<k exist. A known lower-intruder repair consumes {2,4,5}, widens the gap, and exits the original family.
findings.evidence: informal exact arithmetic argument retained in notebook
findings.scope: specified forcing normal form and positive distinct integers
findings.limitations: The packing argument is informal, not Lean-certified here. The forcing-scheme obstruction assumes no lower witness and no upper counter in an exact block, and must handle every structurally permitted witness. It does not rule out semantic branch exclusions or other proof languages. A decreasing counter count alone supplies neither future complements nor terminal closure.
